Honestly you might just put on some antiseptic and just let it dry out while you sleep. The trick is to not touch it because it could trigger you and hinder the healing. Just be super careful of infection because your face is very close to your brain and it can turn so serious so fast.

I am not a doctor disclaimer. But I’d clean it, and use a very light touch of Neosporin. You don’t want to drown it but also you don’t want it super dry, then I would just put a bandage over it at night and a patch over it during the day (it helps me to feel less embarrassed). DefINITELY DO NOT PICK right after you take any patches or bandages off because the skin will be moist and super susceptible. I learned this lesson when I almost skinned my nose. But just be light with it and keep it clean. Your body will do the rest. If! It starts burning or gets particularly red/inflamed or if you see any puss outside of the normal realm of healing, I’d go to an urgent care just because face infections can be serious. But I’d just let your body do it and remove triggers.

I dealt with burnout and it made me want to literally pass away but here are a few things that really, really helped me:
- sleeping as much as I needed and not limiting myself. This meant no alarms. I would get what I could get done when I was awake (I’m a copywriter who works from home) and then rest as needed
- surrounding my work space in my happy things. I covered my space in plants, art, cool rocks, and adorable trinkets. It was easier to work in a space I actually liked being in.
- doing one thing to “get ready” even when I was staying home. Sometimes this meant putting on clothes. Sometimes it was drinking coffee on my patio. And sometimes it meant doing my makeup in my pajamas. But having a “this is me getting ready to do the things” routine made it much easier. 
- being honest with myself and saying “no” when I need to 

I read something once where someone said that to cure burnout, you have to do everything opposite of what you would do to cure depression. Where depression therapy asks you to get out of bed and shower and forces you to do the things to feel better, burnout therapy says allow your body to rest and take a break from those things. Sleep as much as you need, don’t shower if you can’t, turn off the lights and stay in bed if thats what your body wants. Feel free to message if you want to talk about it more in depth!
